angles.label: Front 3/4
angles.why: The hero shot. Best for paint, grille, headlights, body kit and stance.
angles.how: Stand at roughly 45 degrees off the front-left corner, about 3 m away. Camera at wheel-hub height.

angles.label: Side Profile
angles.why: The workhorse. Best for exhaust, seat, wheels, stance, side skirts and decals.
angles.how: Stand exactly perpendicular to the vehicle, about 4 m away. Keep the camera level with the wheel hubs, not tilted down.

angles.label: Rear 3/4
angles.why: Best for tail lights, spoiler, diffuser, exhaust tips and rear fender work.
angles.how: Stand at roughly 45 degrees off the rear-right corner, about 3 m away, camera at hub height.

angles.label: Front Straight
angles.why: Best for headlights, grille, mirrors, handlebar width and front-end symmetry.
angles.how: Stand directly in front, squared up, about 3 m away, camera at headlight height.

rules.text: Plain, uncluttered background - a wall or shutter works best
Even, soft light. Open shade or an overcast sky is ideal
Whole vehicle in frame with a little space around it
Camera held at wheel-hub height, kept level
Landscape orientation, hold the phone sideways
No harsh direct sun creating hard shadows across the body
Do not shoot from above looking down, it distorts proportions
No people, other vehicles or clutter in the frame
Do not crop off the wheels or any part of the vehicle
Avoid heavy zoom or portrait-mode background blur
